sample_unit: readers (each interpreting 150 NCCTH scans unaided and with AI)

links.outcome: Reader sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for critical CT head abnormalities
links.effect: Pooled reader sensitivity rose from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, p<0.001) with AI; specificity fell from 84.5% to 78.9% (-5.5%, p=0.046). ED clinicians with AI matched unaided radiologists' sensitivity.
links.quote: With AI assistance, pooled reader sensitivity for critically abnormal scans increased from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, 95% CI +1.4% to +10.6%, p<0.001), and for intracranial haemorrhage from 84.6% to 91.6% (+7.0%, 95% CI +3.2% to +10.8%, p<0.001), but specificity decreased from 84.5% to 78.9% (–5.5%, 95% CI –11.0% to –0.09%, p=0.046).

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in the reading workflow versus unaided, rather than standalone model metrics
links.effect: AI assistance raised pooled reader sensitivity from 82.8% to 89.7% but lowered specificity from 84.5% to 78.9%; reader confidence AUC did not change significantly.
links.quote: AI-assisted interpretation increased reader sensitivity for critical abnormalities but reduced specificity.

screen.reason: Multireader multicase (MRMC) study evaluating reader performance with and without an AI diagnostic tool; evaluates basic AI assistance rather than testing an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
